description: The National Inventory of Dams is the United States' register of dams, compiled and published by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers under congressional authorisation from the data of state and federal dam-safety regulators and owners. On 26 September 2026 its public feature service held 92,606 dam records. Each record carries 81 attributes: identifiers and names, owner types, the federal and state agencies that regulate, inspect and operate the dam, location with river, county and congressional district, purposes, dam and core types, foundation, several height definitions, length, volume, year completed and years modified, normal, maximum and NID storage, surface and drainage area, maximum discharge, spillway and outlet gates, lock dimensions, last inspection date and frequency, downstream hazard potential, condition assessment, whether an emergency action plan exists and when it was revised, and operational status. Coverage is the United States and its territories, at point resolution, continuously updated record by record. It is open through the NID website (search, map, national CSV export) and an ArcGIS REST feature service, free of charge; no licence text is stated. Caveats: attribute completeness varies by state regulator, some fields are coded values, and the inventory does not include inundation maps or structural design detail. Simulation uses: dam-failure hazard exposure, reservoir and flood-defence system description for resilience models, emergency planning using hazard potential and emergency action plan status, and ageing analysis from construction and inspection dates. It pairs with the National Levee Database for US flood defences and with global dam inventories such as GRanD and Global Dam Watch.
